title: devteam log line
description: One line of the log (process/supervisor.md): planners write project/log/plan-<feature>.jsonl in their worktree (it lands with the plan PR); everyone else writes run/log/<writer>.jsonl live and the supervisor mirrors those into project/log with the chore-log PR. Every line is an envelope plus a body. The envelope is validated by this schema's top level; the body (everything but the envelope keys) by $defs.types[type]: a question's later lines add only its status and reason, the supervisor's rating (stake, urgency, settles, settles_if) and the owner's own fields; x-required-new lists what a new line must carry, x-set-only what may only be set later. x-authority says which writer class may create which types and set which fields; x-id how ids are formed. scripts/devteam.mjs enforces all of it on write and in log-check (a line from a newer kit, with a type or a top-level field this schema doesn't know, is set aside and reported, never an error: it grants nothing), and the cheap part (by matches the file, id names its writer, the authority table, a planner stays inside its own feature) on every read, so a line never grants more than its file's writer has. Three state rules live in the fold because a schema can't state them: a set applies only if no higher-ranked writer set that field; a question is defaulted only if it has a default; the supervisor edits a goal only while it is a draft, or with approved naming an owner-answered goal-change question for that goal not used before.

v.description: Version of the log line format.

id.description: The record's id in the log: a type letter, when it was created, and who wrote it. Tickets and features use their own slug.

type.description: What kind of record this is.

op.description: new creates the record; set changes some of its fields later.

by.description: owner, supervisor, a ticket id, or plan-<feature>; must match the file's writer (owner-<yyyy-mm>, supervisor-<yyyy-mm>, <ticket-id>, plan-<feature>)
by.x-tip: Who wrote the line: you, the supervisor, a ticket's agent or a planner.

channel.description: on owner lines only: where the owner typed it. chat: the owner said it in the supervisor's session and the supervisor recorded it (an answer with the owner's words in said, or the standing rule or goal verdict it carried). thread: the same, from the owner's turn in a thread (answer --from-turn), which the answer names in turn
channel.x-tip: Where you gave it: the dashboard, your terminal, the supervisor's chat, or a thread (recorded with your words).

goal.description: A broad outcome the owner wants. Readings are observations (kind reading, subject = the goal). Preconditions are referred to as <goal-id>#<n>.

title.description: The goal in a few words.

outcome.description: What is true for users or the business when the goal is met.

measure.description: The number that says whether it is met: what is measured, the target, its unit, and whether up or down is better.

target.description: The value that meets the goal.

direction.description: up if higher is better, down if lower is.

source.description: How the fleet reads it: repo (a command the kit runs on main), prod (a read-only command against production) or owner (a yes/no question the owner answers; target 1, unit attested).

check.description: For repo and prod: the command whose last line of output is the number.

question.description: For owner: the yes/no question that says it is met.

link.description: For repo: the repo link whose main the check runs on (absent: home).

horizon.description: The date the goal should be met by, if there is one.

non_goals.description: What this goal deliberately leaves out.

preconditions.description: What must be true before the goal can be met; features are planned to make each one true.

registry_precondition.description: The number (1-based) of the precondition that is "the registry is complete" (planning.md §7). goal-readiness for this goal waits for the owner's yes to a registry-attest question about it. Set by goal add|set --registry-precondition n; null clears it. The check reads this field, never a precondition's wording.
registry_precondition.x-tip: Which precondition is "the registry is complete": marking ready waits for your yes that the registry lists everything.

priority.description: Its order among the goals: 1 comes first.

milestones.description: The goal's outcome in order, each a usable slice with a target on the goal's measure, the preconditions it makes true (1-based), an optional date and a rough size in tickets. Written from the design; the last target is the goal's. Referred to as <goal-id>@<n>.

title.description: The milestone in a few words.

target.description: The value of the goal's measure that reaches it.

by.description: The date it should be reached by, if you set one.

preconditions.description: The goal's preconditions it makes true, by number.

tickets.description: A rough size, in tickets, before it is planned.

milestones.x-tip: The goal in usable slices, in order: each with a target on its measure, the preconditions it makes true, and an optional date.

status.description: draft while it is being defined, ready once you approve it, met when the measure reaches its target, abandoned when let go.

kind.description: upkeep: the built-in goal that owns the reserved chores feature and the supervisor's upkeep (planning.md §7). It has no measure, design, milestones or status lifecycle; the earliest upkeep line is the one, later ones are ignored.
kind.x-tip: upkeep for the built-in goal that owns chores and the supervisor's upkeep; empty for every other goal.

hold.description: The goal's toggle (planning.md §1, holds): run, drain (nothing new starts; in-flight work finishes and merges) or park (sessions commit WIP, push, write a handoff and stop; ticket merges wait). fleet names the fleet op that set it and prior the hold it replaced, so fleet undrain/unpark can put it back. The owner sets any hold; a supervisor line counts only as a drain of a running goal, the release of its own drain, or a fleet op (the fold enforces it).

host.description: The machine a fleet op ran on, so the moved fleet's supervisor knows whether it is on the old machine or the new one.

hold.x-tip: The goal's toggle: run, drain (nothing new starts, work in flight finishes) or park (sessions stop with a handoff).

decision.description: The owner's latest decision on the goal: approve (ready), refine (notes the planner takes into account before asking again), let-go (abandoned), restore (a let-go goal back to the status it had, parked), met (the owner's yes to a goal-met question, named in question, marked it met).
decision.x-tip: Your latest verdict on its design: approve, refine, let go or restore.

plan_after.description: Goals whose design this goal's design waits on, each with why. The only reason to leave a goal that needs planning without a planner; it lapses once that goal is approved. Empty to plan in parallel.
plan_after.x-tip: Goals whose design this one waits on, and why.

approved.description: on a supervisor's set of a goal past draft: the goal-change question (its id) the owner answered with the recommendation. The set must be exactly the change that question proposed; each answer authorises one set.
approved.x-tip: The goal-change question whose answer authorised the supervisor's latest change.

carried.description: On a supervisor's set with approved: the answer was given before goal-change questions recorded their change, and the supervisor carries it forward (a carry-answer act the owner can correct).
carried.x-tip: The supervisor carried an older answer of yours forward to make this change.

feature.description: A feature on the roadmap: the goals it serves, the goal preconditions it makes true, its stories and their target releases, and the design it implements. Its id is the feature slug. A feature is approved when its lines are on main (they land with the plan/<feature> PR). The reserved feature "chores" has no object.

title.description: The feature in a few words.

preconditions.description: The goal preconditions this feature makes true (<goal-id>#<n>).

stories.description: What users can do once it ships, each with the release it targets.

id.description: The story's id: the component's prefix and S with a number.

text.description: What a user can do once it ships.

links.description: Registry links (settings.md links) every ticket of this feature needs, by id.

notes.description: Anything else the planner wanted on record.

ticket.description: One PR of work. Its id is <component>-<NN>-<slug>. A re-plan is a set (superseded_by, depends_on, touches …).

title.description: The ticket in a few words.

feature.description: The feature it is part of (chores for upkeep).

component.description: The part of the codebase it belongs to.

kind.description: contract (an interface others build on), build, integration, chore, spike (a time-boxed investigation) or fix (a production incident, from a decision in incident-fix).

size.description: S or M: tickets are kept small enough for one PR.

risk.description: high gets two reviewers and a full plan read; normal is approved from its TL;DR and plan review.

depends_on.description: Tickets that must merge before this one starts.

contracts.description: Interfaces it provides to other tickets, and ones it consumes.

touches.description: The files and folders it may change; two tickets in flight never overlap.

touches_components.description: On a contract or integration ticket: other components in the same repo whose lines its touches may fall in (planning.md D2, D7).

links.description: Registry links (settings.md links) this ticket's worker needs, by id; they join its prompt's Links block.

done_when.description: What must be true for it to count as done.

one_way_doors.description: Choices in it that are hard to undo; you answer each before its plan is approved.

superseded_by.description: The ticket that replaced it in a re-plan.

held.description: Why the supervisor is not scheduling this ticket yet; null releases it. A held ticket is left out of `ready` and the idle-capacity finding.
held.x-tip: Why the supervisor is not scheduling it yet; empty once released.

notes.description: Anything else the planner wanted on record.

phase.description: A worker's phase change, or a liveness ping (from = to), with cumulative spend. A worker's last line of any type is its last sign of life. The supervisor records its own spend with to: supervisor. A planner logs only parked (when drained) and starting (written for it when it is started again).

to.description: The phase the agent moved to.

task.description: The step of its plan it is on.

note.description: What it said about the move.

usd.description: What it had spent so far, in dollars.

gate.description: One run of a gate (lint, test, …): duration, result, commit, and the failed and slowest tests.

ms.description: How long it took, in milliseconds.

dirty.description: The run had uncommitted changes, so sha does not name what ran (a TDD red, then green). Not counted for flakiness.
dirty.x-tip: The run had uncommitted changes, so it is not counted toward flakiness.

tests.description: Per-test results, for flaky and slow tests.

preexisting.description: A ratchet gate that failed here and at the merge base too: pre-existing debt, allowed; not counted in the gate's fail rate.
preexisting.x-tip: It failed on main too: existing debt, allowed, not counted against the check.

repo.description: The repo link the gate ran in, for a ticket outside home (absent: home).
repo.x-tip: The repo this check ran in, when not this one.

message.description: A one-line message typed into another session's pane. A reply names the message it answers in re.

kind.description: What sort of message: a question for a review or go-ahead, a merge request, blocked, a design change, a ruling, a relayed answer, or info.

observation.description: Something noticed: a metrics finding, a slow test, a goal reading (kind reading), a trial's outcome (kind outcome), an escaped defect, a retro (kind retro, source_ref = its file), a week's learning record (kind learning: its week and figures). Deduped on source_key.

source.description: Who or what noticed it, as its writer gave it: a sensor's name on a sensor's line, repo, prod or owner on a goal reading, one of x-ooda.sources from observe --source, or older free text. Free text stays valid; where it came from, in x-ooda.sources words, is computed when it is read (provenance).

subject.description: What it is about: a ticket, component, feature, gate, goal, class or record.

kind.description: What sort of observation (a reading, a slow test, an escaped defect, a retro…).

detector.description: The check that found it: sensor and metrics mark the kit's own lines (every kit reads them so), pane the kit's pane check; anything else is free text.

source_key.description: Groups repeats of the same signal together.

release.description: An exception's release, as its sensor validated it.

source_ref.description: The file or record it came from.

week.description: On a learning record (kind learning): the ISO week it counts, in UTC, as yyyy-Www. Its at is when it was written, which for a back-filled week is later.

figures.description: On a learning record (kind learning): the week's counts, from the log as it stood at the week's end. Counts, never shares: the views divide.
figures.x-tip: What the week counted: informed, autonomous, trusted.

informed.description: Informed: what the loop knew at the week's end.
informed.x-tip: Whether the agents work from what the loop has learned.

knowledge.description: Accepted knowledge in force at the week's end.

signals_formed.description: Recurring signals formed by the week's end (three or more on one key, from two writers or on two days).

signals_explained.description: Of those, the ones a lesson, a problem, an incident or a live decision explains.

starts.description: Workers and planners started fresh in the week.

starts_given.description: Of those, the ones whose prompt carried at least one lesson.

autonomous.description: Autonomous: how much the supervisor did alone.
autonomous.x-tip: Whether the supervisor needs to ask less.

ladder_calls.description: Calls in a trust-ladder class made in the week.

trusted_calls.description: Of those, the ones made on trust (its rung, or a standing rule) rather than asked.

questions.description: Decisions put to the owner in the week (decisions, one-way doors, proposals, trust, clarifications).

trusted.description: Trusted: how often the owner agreed, and corrected.
trusted.x-tip: Whether the owner agrees with the supervisor's calls.

answered.description: Questions the owner answered in the week that carried a recommendation.

agreed.description: Of those, the ones answered with the recommendation.

calls.description: The supervisor's calls made in the week.

corrections.description: Corrections the owner made in the week.

sha.description: A reading of a repo measure: the commit on main its check ran on.

approved.description: A reading of an owner measure the supervisor records: the goal-met question the owner answered yes.

measure.description: The value it read, with its unit.

link.description: On a link observation: the resource the work depends on, as the owner or a worker gave it (the supervisor folds these into the registry, settings.md links).

url.description: https only, and never with credentials (no user or token before an @ in the host)

title.description: One line of plain text, at most 120 characters: no line breaks, tabs, or control or bidi characters (it reaches workers' prompts).

notes.description: One line of plain text, at most 500 characters, as the title.

knowledge.description: What the project has learned. Accepted entries whose scope matches go into the prompts of the sessions they apply to.

kind.description: fact, lesson, preference (often a standing rule of yours), constraint or pointer.

scope.description: Where it applies: the whole project, a component, a feature, a kind of decision, a chore, or a link (link:<id>: wherever that link is in the prompt).

status.description: candidate until you keep it; accepted ones go into the instructions of every agent they apply to; stale or retired ones no longer do.

confidence.description: How sure whoever proposed it was, 0 to 1.

evidence.description: The records it was learned from.

owner_note.description: The owner's refinement of the lesson, given when they keep it: prompts show it with the statement. Only the owner's own lines carry it.

kit_lesson.description: The supervisor's own tag on knowledge it wrote: this looks like it would hold for any project on the kit, so the box's operator reads it first when it looks for an upstream change. It grants nothing: no prompt, status, approval or trust reads it. Only the supervisor's lines carry it, and only on its own entries.

problem.description: Something wrong (realized) or that could go wrong (a risk), with a lifecycle. An incident is a problem the sensors found: it holds their fingerprints, and its severity is computed from their observations.

title.description: The problem in a few words.

realized.description: true for an issue that is happening, false for a risk that might.

status.description: open, owned, mitigating, verifying (a fix is out, inside its verify window) or resolved.

detail.description: What is wrong and what is known.

fingerprints.description: An incident's fingerprints: <sensor>:<kind>:<fingerprint>, as sensor triage lists them.

sensor.description: The sensor whose fingerprints an incident holds first.

verify.description: An incident's fix in production: the merge commit, its verify window (from, until), whether the deploy was matched or assumed, whether it resolved unverified, and the commits whose fix regressed.

commit.description: The merge commit of the fix.

until.description: The end of the verify window.

assumed.description: true when no deploy event matched the commit and the window started deploy_lag_minutes after the merge.

from.description: When the verify window started: the deploy, or deploy_lag_minutes after the merge.

unverified.description: true when it resolved with its fingerprints seen fewer than 3 times.

regressed.description: Merge commits whose fix didn't hold.

seen.description: How many times its fingerprints had been seen when the window started.

question.description: The supervisor asking the owner. why_asked says the class, its rung and ceiling, and the reasons. The owner's answer (a set) may carry an autonomy direction and a standing rule; an answer equal to the recommendation counts as agreement. stake, urgency, settles and settles_if are the supervisor's rating: it may set them again while the question is open, and they are left out of the hash the owner's answer records, so a new rating never reopens an answered question.

kind.description: What sort of question: a decision, a one-way door, a clarification, a proposal, more trust, defining or approving a goal, something only you can do, or a review.

class.description: The kind of decision on the trust ladder it belongs to.

scope.description: Narrows the class to one area, if set.

thread.description: The thread it was asked in (thread ask): it shows there and in the Inbox, and is answered once, in either.
thread.x-tip: The thread with the supervisor this was asked in.

choices.description: The possible answers, recommended one included (name it in recommendation by its label): a short label, what it means, and what it changes for the product's users.
choices.x-tip: The answers offered: a label, what it means, and what it changes for users.

secrets.description: Values an owner-action question asks the owner to post, each with where it goes. The value is piped from the owner's process straight to its sink and never written to the log (supervisor.md, owner actions).
secrets.x-tip: Values it asked you to post, and where each goes. Values never reach the log.

secrets_posted.description: Which declared secrets the owner has posted, cumulative: the name and when. Never the value or its size.
secrets_posted.x-tip: Which secrets you posted, and when. Never the values.

links.description: What the owner must look at to answer (a spec, a plan, a mock): a path in the repo at ref (default main), a URL, a registry link by id, an artifact by slug, or a preview by name.

link.description: A registry link's id (settings.md links); the inbox shows its locator.

artifact.description: An artifact's slug (project/artifacts/<slug>/); the dashboard opens it in its viewer.

preview.description: A preview's name (devteam.mjs preview list); the dashboard links it for this machine and shows whether it is up.

at.description: Where the artifact was when asked: main (landed) or the worktree drawing it.

sha256.description: The artifact's fingerprint when asked, written by ask; the dashboard says when it has changed since.

blob.description: On a strategy-change question's link to project/strategy.md: the git blob of the draft when asked, written by ask (which also resolves ref to that commit). merge lands exactly this text under the owner's answer.

name.description: A short key, unique in the question; its text and context name the link inline as [[name]].

links.x-tip: What to look at to answer: files in the repo, URLs, or artifacts.

rule_scope.description: Where a standing rule given with the answer applies, unless the owner names another scope (chore:devteam-sync for an upstream sync approval).
rule_scope.x-tip: Where a standing rule given with the answer applies.

goal.description: The goal a goal-approval question asks the owner to approve, on its linked design.

confidence.description: How sure the supervisor was of its recommendation, 0 to 1.

default.description: What happens if you do not answer by the deadline (only where the class allows one).

blocks.description: Tickets or chores waiting on the answer; or, for an incident-fix question, the incident (p-…) it is about.

stake.description: How much of what the fleet does next changes with the answer: 3 one answer stops or redirects a goal, a milestone or a feature; 2 the answers lead to different designs or plans; 1 a detail. For something only the owner can do (owner-action): what can't go ahead without it, 3 a goal or milestone, 2 a feature, 1 one ticket. The supervisor rates it; the kit orders the Inbox from it and never stores the order.
stake.x-tip: How much rides on your answer: 3 the work itself, 2 its design, 1 a detail.

urgency.description: How soon waiting costs: 3 work is stopped on it now; 2 work will stop on it before the current milestone is done; 1 nothing waits yet. A 3 counts as 3 only while blocks names a ticket that is waiting or an open incident, or the question has a default; otherwise it counts as 2.
urgency.x-tip: How soon it matters: 3 work is stopped now, 2 soon, 1 nothing waits yet.

settles.description: Open questions one answer to this one (settles_if) would make unnecessary. Counted only while this question is stake 3 and shares a goal or feature with each. It is ordered above them; the supervisor withdraws them when the owner gives that answer.
settles.x-tip: Questions that one of these answers would close.

settles_if.description: The answer that settles them: a choice's label where there are choices.

approves.description: The acts this question approves, named when asked (ask --approves): ticket ids, chore-<slug> or plan-<feature>. The answer approves each once and nothing else.
approves.x-tip: The tickets, chores or plans its answer approves, each once.

why_asked.description: Why it came to you: the rung and ceiling of its class, and the reasons.

status.description: withdrawn or defaulted; an answered question carries your answer instead.

said.description: the owner's own words, verbatim, when the answer came through the supervisor's chat or from the owner's turn in a thread
said.x-tip: Your words, verbatim, when you answered in the supervisor's chat.

turn.description: On an answer recorded from a thread (answer --from-turn): the owner's turn whose words are in said. One turn settles one question.
turn.x-tip: The message in a thread your answer came from.

autonomy.description: What your answer said about the next decision of this class: ask, ask with a default, or decide and tell you.

standing_rule.description: A rule you gave with the answer, kept as knowledge.

sensor.description: the sensor this owner-action question asks a credential for, so discovery asks once

remediation.description: The remediation a production-remediation question was asked about, pinned when asked: its name, sha and entry_hash. remediate refuses if the entry has changed.

remediation_entries.description: The remediation entries a governance-edit question would approve (name, script, sha, entry_hash; ask --remediations). merge lands a change only if it is one of these, exactly.

owner_said.description: The owner's words, verbatim, when a question asks again after their no. Checked against the transcript like a chat answer's said.

re.description: the worker message this question escalates

met.description: On a goal-met question (ask writes it): the goal as asked, basis (a hash of its title, measure and milestones), and the reading the question shows (null for an owner-read goal, whose yes is the reading). The owner's yes marks the goal met only while its basis is still this, after a repo or prod check reads it again.
met.x-tip: The goal as it was when asked, and the reading the question showed.

change.description: On a goal-change question about a goal: the exact goal fields it proposes. The owner's answer with the recommendation authorises this change and no other (goal set --approved applies it as is).
change.x-tip: The exact change to the goal it proposed; your answer authorised that and nothing else.

review.description: A review question's pinned files (process/supervisor.md): the agent's page, its optional data and the result's optional schema, read at one commit, each with its sha256 and size; data counts its rows and the rows with a proposal. The owner's process re-hashes them before it accepts a result. A review is answered with its result (answer --review-result) or sent back (answer --decline), never with free text or a default.
review.x-tip: The pages and data you reviewed, pinned by hash.

result.description: On the owner's answer to a review: the sha256 and size of run/questions/<qid>/result.json as the owner's process wrote it and, for a result in the standard rows shape, the counts it recomputed: proposed is the rows whose data has a proposal; kept the decided rows whose values equal it (never taken from the page); cleared the other decided rows with every value empty; changed the rest.
result.x-tip: Your review result, by hash, with how many rows you kept, changed or cleared.

declined.description: On the owner's answer to a review: sent back without a result; the answer says why.
declined.x-tip: You sent the review back without a result.

question_hash.description: On the owner's answer: the hash of the question as the owner saw it (every field it was asked with). An answer whose question no longer has this hash answers nothing: the question was changed after the owner answered it, so it is open again.
question_hash.x-tip: The question as you saw it when you answered.

decision.description: What the supervisor decided and under what trust: the class and scope, the options it weighed, why, and the authority it acted on, snapshotted when it decided (the class's rung and ceiling, and the owner's answer, default or standing rule it rests on). Acts that carry it out cite it with decision. Trust is earned and lost on decisions: a correction on a decision drops its class to rung 1. The owner, or the supervisor at a retro, sets corrected; the supervisor then sets repaired.

class.description: The kind of decision on the trust ladder.

scope.description: Narrows the class to one area, if set.

confidence.description: How sure the supervisor was, 0 to 1.

impact.description: On a goal-impact decision: how much the goal (refs[0]) matters to the project, judged against project/strategy.md: 4 the project depends on it, 3 moves a number the project watches, 2 worth having, 1 housekeeping.
impact.x-tip: How much the goal matters: 4 the project depends on it, 3 moves a number it watches, 2 worth having, 1 housekeeping.

refs.description: What it is about; acts under it stay within these.

rung.description: The class's rung when it was decided: 1 asks, 2 asks with a default, 3 decides and tells you.

ceiling.description: The highest rung the class can reach.

authority.description: rung: the class's rung let the supervisor act alone; answer: an owner's answer (approved_by) approved it; default: a question's default applied; standing-rule: a knowledge ruling (approved_by k-...) covers it; constitution: a class the ladder doesn't hold, acted on under the constitution's own terms
authority.x-tip: What allowed the call: its rung, your answer, a default, a standing rule, or the constitution.

approved_by.description: Your answer or standing rule it rests on.

knowledge.description: The knowledge or problems this decision rests on (decide --on); never copied into refs, and never its authority (approved_by is).
knowledge.x-tip: The lessons, facts or problems the call rests on.

corrected.description: Your correction, if the call was wrong; it drops the class to rung 1. On a goal-impact decision (constitutional, so no rung drops) it may carry the impact you give the goal instead.

impact.description: On the owner's correction of a goal-impact decision: the impact the owner gives the goal. It stands until the owner changes it.

repaired.description: What the supervisor did about the correction.

act.description: Something the supervisor did (incl. approve-spec, approve-plan, merge-word, and worker-slots, whose planner acts carry the feature's id_block). An act that carries decision did what that decision line decided, and the decision answers for it: the owner corrects the decision, not the act. An act without decision is its own decision (mechanical acts, and every act written before decisions existed). The owner, or the supervisor at a retro, sets corrected; the supervisor then sets repaired. The owner writes acts of one class only, artifact-publish (devteam.mjs artifact publish|unpublish, which the cloud gateway's confirm page runs): the record of what the owner made public, with artifact and, for a publish, tree. It is a record, never a call: trust, decisions and corrections leave it out, and only the owner writes that class.

class.description: The kind of act or decision.

scope.description: Narrows the class to one area, if set.

rung.description: The class's rung when it acted on its own trust.

approved_by.description: Your answer or standing rule it rests on.

decision.description: The decision line this act carries out (d-...). The act then takes its class and authority from it.

knowledge.description: On a worker-slots act that started a worker or planner fresh: the accepted knowledge its prompt carried (the knowledge that applies to its ticket or feature), newest first, at most 60. Never in what, which the kit parses. A resumed session reads no new prompt, so its act carries none.
knowledge.x-tip: The lessons and facts its instructions carried when it started.

corrected.description: Your correction, if it was its own call and wrong.

repaired.description: What the supervisor did about the correction.

id_block.description: On the act that made a planner: the ticket numbers (the NN of <component>-NN-<slug>, from..to inclusive) reserved for its feature, above every number on main, in a plan in flight, and in every earlier block. validate on plan/<feature> warns about a ticket of the feature outside it; merge --plan refuses an id already on main.
id_block.x-tip: The ticket numbers reserved for a planner's feature.

entry_hash.description: On a registry-edit act (link add|set|rm), or a governance-edit or gate-change act from link … --approved: the link entry it wrote, as sha256:<hex> of its canonical JSON, or null when it removed the link. merge lands a change to a url link only when an act naming the link recorded exactly the entry that lands, and a change to a repo link only when an act of the --approved answer naming the link did. An act without it (written before it existed) never matches.
entry_hash.x-tip: The link entry this act wrote.

prior_hash.description: On a registry-edit act (link add|set|rm), or a governance-edit or gate-change act from link … --approved: the link entry it replaced (for an --approved act, the entry main had), as sha256:<hex> of its canonical JSON, or null when it added the link. merge lands a change to a url link only when acts naming the link lead from the entry main has (prior_hash) to the one that lands (entry_hash), and link land carries an entry only on the same terms, so an act made from an entry main has since changed (a stale set, an rm of an earlier entry) never lands. An act without it (written before it existed) never matches.
prior_hash.x-tip: The link entry this act replaced.

repo.description: The repo link the act was about (a merge, a release), when not home.
repo.x-tip: The repo this was in, when not this one.

artifact.description: On the owner's artifact-publish act: the slug of the landed artifact (project/artifacts/<slug>/) published or taken down.
artifact.x-tip: The artifact you published or took down.

tree.description: On the owner's artifact-publish act with what publish: the git tree id of the artifact's folder on main that the gateway checked byte for byte and serves. Absent on an unpublish.

spend.description: What agents spent, observed from their harnesses' session logs by the supervisor's tick: one line per agent and phase, covering its responses up to `through` since its previous spend line. The log keeps spend durable after the harness's own logs are gone.

who.x-tip: The ticket, planner or supervisor that spent it.

phase.description: The phase the spend was in.

through.description: ISO time of the latest response counted

cache_read_tokens.description: Tokens read from the prompt cache.

cache_write_tokens.description: Tokens written to the prompt cache.

thread.description: A conversation between the owner and the supervisor about one thing the owner pointed at (its subject), or about nothing in particular (started from the dock). Only the owner starts one; its messages are turn lines, and a question asked in it carries thread. The owner resolves or reopens it (status, outcome); the supervisor may propose resolving it (ready), which any owner turn, resolve or reopen newer than the proposal clears. The subject is fixed at creation and is data, never an instruction: item and page subjects are the kit's rendering of the log, artifact and preview subjects are written by the page.

title.description: One line naming what the owner pointed at, as the page showed it, or the owner's first words for a thread with no subject.

subject.description: What the owner pointed at: kind item (a record the dashboard drew, by ref), page (a spot on a dashboard view), artifact (a point on an artifact) or preview (an element in a running dev app). Each kind carries only its own keys, each string within its cap in bytes, at most 2,500 bytes encoded (scripts/devteam.mjs subjectProblem).

quote.description: item and page: the text the page showed for it (at most 300 bytes).

at.description: page: {x, y} as fractions of the section's box. artifact: where it was shown (main, a worktree, or tree:<id>).

anchor.description: artifact and preview: the element (selector, tag, role, text, name, html, rect, and the point inside it).

point.description: artifact and preview: {x, y} in the frame, when no element could be read.

errors.description: preview: the last console errors (at most 3 of 200 bytes).

subject.x-tip: The thing you pointed at, as the page had it.

status.description: open or resolved: the owner's. A reopen is a status open line; its history is the set lines.

outcome.description: The owner's line on how it ended (at most 300 bytes), or null for none.

ready.description: The supervisor's proposal to resolve it, with the outcome it suggests. The owner never writes it (the fold's writer ranks would then lock the supervisor out of it); an owner line newer than it clears it.

outcome.description: The outcome it proposes, one line, at most 300 bytes.

ready.x-tip: The supervisor's suggestion that it is done.

turn.description: One message in a thread: the owner's words to the supervisor, which carry the weight of the owner's words in its session and are already verbatim here, or the supervisor's reply. Never changed. A turn on a thread that doesn't exist or is resolved is refused by thread say (the owner's) and thread reply (the supervisor's).

thread.x-tip: The thread it was said in.

text.description: What was said: at most 2,000 bytes of UTF-8, several lines allowed.

refs.description: On a supervisor turn: what it did or is about, as <type>:<id> (goal:g-…, ticket:checkout-04, act:a-…), at most 8 of 120 bytes. question:<qid> names an Inbox question asked in this thread, so the owner's next turn may settle it (answer --from-turn).

question.description: On a supervisor turn: the question this turn asks, an Inbox question carrying this thread (thread ask).

x-ooda.description: Where each record sits in the loop (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act, Learn), and the words for where an observation came from. The views compute both when they read a record (stageOf, provenanceOf in scripts/devteam.mjs); nothing stores them, so a line an older kit wrote reads the same. A measurement (a reading, spend, a gate) is outside the loop: it is never a signal Orient groups. inbox: a question, drawn in Decide as the owner's call once answered. A type not listed (the work graph, conversation) has no stage.
x-ooda.x-tip: The five stages of the loop: what was noticed, what is known, what was decided, what was done, and what was learned.

x-source-words.sensor: a production sensor, or a goal's measure
x-source-words.owner-chat: what you said in the supervisor's chat
